sections.html:
Washington County's Hurricane forms the eastern edge of the St. George metro area. It has one ZIP code, 84737, and the 435 area code. Residents numbered 20,036 at the 2020 count and roughly 25,745 by July 2025, a jump of 45.7% between 2010 and 2020. Of 8,035 housing units, 13.1% were vacant in 2020, so a house sitting empty is a common story here.

All that growth means new construction close by. A resale often competes with brand-new homes, and some owners of older houses would rather sell as they are than fight that comparison.

Summers are brutal. St. George, the closest long-term weather station, averages a July high near 102 degrees, and about 60 afternoons a year hit 100 or more. Freezing mornings at or below 32 degrees happen about 60 times a year too, while rain totals only about 9 inches. Monsoon season starts around mid-July and runs into mid-September, bringing patchy thunderstorms.

Roofing and cooling equipment age fast in that heat, so buyers will want to know how old yours are. Check the drainage around the lot after a storm. The Quail Creek dike failure on January 1, 1989 shows that water has caused serious damage in this area before.

The city operates its own electric utility. The Hurricane Valley Fire District covers fire protection, and Hurricane High School, serving grades 10 to 12, belongs to the Washington County School District.

You can reach city offices at 147 N 870 W or by calling 435-635-2811. Business licensing is handled inside Planning and Zoning, and a home-based business can be approved under Title 10, Chapter 42 of the city code.

A short-term rental in Hurricane needs a business license, and single-family zones have a cap on how many are issued. Section 3-10-11 of the city code holds the details.

RuleHurricane requirement
License cap, single-family zonesThree licenses per 1,000 residents
SpacingNo other permitted rental within 300 feet
ParkingOne off-street space per bedroom
OccupancyTen, unless the fire district approves more with suppression
Complaint responseWithin one hour
FinesUp to $750 per violation, and each day counts

A rental permit belongs to the owner, not the property. A purchaser gets 45 days to apply for a fresh one, and missing that window forfeits it, leaving the new owner to reapply or wait on the list. If the house has been a rental, tell prospective buyers early, since an investor may be paying partly for that permit.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and delinquency
sections.html:
Washington County wants the year's real property tax by November 30 whether or not a notice reached you. If neighbors got theirs and you did not, ring the Treasurer for a copy. The office sets up no payment plans, but any partial payment of $10 or more per parcel is welcome at any time.

  • A payment covers interest first, then penalty, then tax. If several years are behind, Utah law credits the newest year first.
  • The Clerk-Auditor auctions parcels in May once they have been delinquent for five years or longer.
  • Utah bans the sale of tax liens and tax lien certificates.

Unpaid tax is a lien on the land, not on a person, and for a mid-year sale the title company splits the bill between the two sides. Find the Treasurer at 111 East Tabernacle St. in St. George, or call 435-301-7720.

sections.h2: Appeals and the primary residence exemption
sections.html: State law sets the valuation appeal deadline: the later of September 15 or 45 days after the auditor sends notice. The primary residence exemption leaves a main home taxed on 55% of market value. After a sale, the buyer files a new claim to keep it.

sections.h2: What happens at closing in Hurricane?
sections.html:
Closing takes place at a title company, which files the deed with the Washington County Recorder at 111 East Tabernacle in St. George. Anything arriving after 4:45 p.m. Mountain Time is turned away, and the Recorder answers at 435-301-7680.

Utah law wants the deed to name the grantees, include a mailing address for tax billing and carry a proper legal description. The seller's signature must match the owner of record, which is worth confirming early on an inherited house.

  1. Put your acceptance of the offer on paper.
  2. Title staff review the record and list every claim against the house, including back taxes or a mortgage.
  3. Sign at the title office, or by mail if you live elsewhere now.
  4. After the deed is recorded, your proceeds are sent out.

Without a loan or appraisal in the way, how fast you close depends mainly on the title work.

An agent listing, a sale by owner and a cash offer are the three paths. A listing means getting the house show-ready while new builds compete down the road, and a cash offer accepts the house exactly as it sits.

  • Empty houses that still carry tax, utility and insurance costs.
  • Short-term rentals that lost a permit or fell short of the city rules.
  • Inherited houses with out-of-state heirs.
  • Older homes with aging roofs, evaporative coolers or failing air conditioning.

From any buyer, ask for a closing date and proof of funds in writing, then compare the number with a listing's net after repairs and commission. Dig out the deed, the latest tax notice and any rental permit paperwork before you start calling around.

A short stack of documents saves days. Pull the recorded deed and the newest tax notice, plus a payoff statement if a loan remains. Receipts for roof or cooler repairs help, as do city permits and, for a former rental, its license paperwork. When the house came to you through a will or trust, bring those papers so the title company can confirm who may sign. A buyer who sees all this can price the house fast, and your closing date is less likely to drift. Ask the title officer what else the county needs before closing is scheduled.

sections.h2: If you own from out of state
sections.html:
Plenty of Hurricane houses belong to heirs or investors living elsewhere. Title companies routinely close by mail with notarized signatures, so there is no need to travel. Give the title officer a list of every co-owner right away, and send identification and notary pages in advance so the closing date holds.

Vacant houses add monthly costs: utilities, insurance and upkeep continue even when no one lives there. Once a cash sale closes, those bills stop, and nobody local has to run showings, meet contractors or watch the property in the meantime.

faqs.a: It was 20,036 at the 2020 census, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 25,745.

faqs.q: When is property tax due in Hurricane?
faqs.a: November 30, billed by the Washington County Treasurer even if no notice arrived. There are no payment plans, but partial payments of $10 or more are taken.

faqs.q: Does a short-term rental license transfer when I sell my Hurricane house?
faqs.a: No. A buyer applies for a new license within 45 days of purchase or it is forfeited, and may then face a waiting list.

faqs.q: Is Hurricane's climate hard on houses?
faqs.a: It can be. Nearby St. George averages a July high near 102 degrees, with about 60 days a year at 100 or above, which wears on roofs, cooling systems and exterior finishes.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for a Hurricane house?
faqs.a: With the Washington County Recorder in St. George, which refuses filings after 4:45 p.m. Mountain Time. Your title company normally files for you.
